newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-VOGTS CALLS FOR ENGLAND TO SCRAP WORLD CUP BID.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-VOGTS CALLS FOR ENGLAND TO SCRAP WORLD CUP BID.

text.p: Germany coach Berti Vogts called on English soccer officials to withdraw their bid for the 2006 World Cup finals because they did not have the support of the whole of Europe.
Speaking after former World Cup coach and captain Franz Beckenbauer attacked the English F.A. on Tuesday, Vogts said: "If I was the Prime Minister of Britain I would tell the F.A. to withdraw.
"If they have any character, they will pull out. All the countries in Europe think that."
The Germans launched their cup campaign in 1993 under the impression that the English F.A. would support them as Europe's leading candidate.
But the English body decided to run a rival bid after last year's succesful staging of the European championship finals.
Beckenbauer was applauded at the presentation, attended by UEFA officials and leading German players, when he criticised the English F.A.
"The English have left us in the lurch. We expected the English to support us. This has got nothing to do with English fair play," Beckenbauer said.
"The English have been a very important motor in the develepment of world football and I have good relations with the English. That was why I was very disappointed.
"The English themselves are okay, but the Football Association has to look at whether it is in order."
FIFA does not decide until the year 2000 which country will host the finals. Rival bids are also expected from South America and Africa.
The Germans are very worried that Europe will miss out if they have two bids.
After the gala Germany captain Juergen Klinsman said it would be "logical" for the English to withdraw if indeed they had give their support to the German bid before.

"Germany helped England a lot to get Europe '96. We don't know what the officials said to each other. It would be a fair move for the English (to withdraw). It would be a disaster for both countries. Both could only lose from that."
